title: harden(metadata): a permission set's name is unique across packages
body:
domain:devx#1 · sunhaolin · session_017xRBcVy4VXmkQjn2MGeaWk

harden(metadata): a permission set's name is unique across packages

Dispatched by the W3-C3b QA run security path (detail withheld). Reworked on the contract-tier review FAIL (PR comment 6497768595): the must-fix and all five should-fixes are taken, each listed under What changes.

Clause-②: no (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none — the published skills teach that a grant references a permission set by its machine `name` (`skills/objectstack-data/rules/security.md`); none claims a name may be reused across owners, so this hardening contradicts nothing, and `Metadata-protocol: none` means there is no new authorable capability to teach.

This narrows a published accept set (a metadata-door write that answered `200` is now refused), so it owes one contract-review-tier review before the queue.

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:权限集(permission set)在元数据的保存门(草稿/直接发布)、"草稿→发布"提升门、以及恢复门(回滚 rollback / 提交回退 revert)上,若同名权限集已被另一个所有者(另一个包,或环境本身)持有,一律拒绝写入,且什么都不落库;错误信封与注册表在安装、冷启动时对同一规则的答复一致:`NAMESPACE_CONFLICT` / 422。
- 为什么改:授权按名字引用权限集(一个名字只能对应一套权限,ADR-0131 D4;裁决 #15196 Q4=A、#22307 A:"一个名字一个持有者,每条路径都如此")。安装与冷启动早已拒绝第二个持有者,元数据入口没有,留下一个与已声明契约不符的缺口。本次返工修正了复审指出的问题:所属包自己用"不带包名的草稿保存"编辑自家权限集时被误拒。属安全加固。
- 风险与回滚:只拦"用别人已占用的名字再写一份"这类本就非法的写入;同一所有者改自己的集照常(包括不带包名的草稿保存、以及历史遗留的"包行旁的无包行");已有两个所有者同名的部署,在改名或删除其中一份之前,对该名字的写入(含 `os migrate meta --stored --apply` 重存、包复制 duplicate 中未带前缀的集)会报失败。回滚 = 还原本 PR。
- 先看:`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save-door-refusals.ts`(判据 `permissionSetNameCollisionRefusal` 与注册表读法 `registryPackageHoldersOf`);`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` 保存门里计算 `landsIn` 的那段(按写入真正落入的包判定,风险最高);`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-authoring-gate.ts` 恢复门的一行调用。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol exec vitest run src/protocol.permission-set-name-cross-package.test.ts` → 预期 17/17 绿(三道门的拒绝 + 各自对照,含"所属包不带包名的草稿编辑可保存"一条)。
- 需要你做的:无 — 席位落地;入队前需一次契约复审档(contract-review)复核,因为本卡 `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`。

## What changes

A permission set's name is its identity across the whole deployment: a grant (`sys_user_permission_set.permission_set`) resolves its set by that name alone (ADR-0131 D4), and positions, permission sets and capabilities each hold one name per deployment (ruling Q4 = A on #15196, record 6050490870). The registry already refuses a second holder at install and at cold boot with `NAMESPACE_CONFLICT` / 422 (ruling A on #22307, record 6063176077: one name, one holder, on every path). The metadata doors keyed a permission-set write by `(type, name, package)` and so let a second owner write a name already held. This PR closes those doors, pulling them back to the already-declared contract (ADR-0086 D4: a package never writes into a record another owns).

`permissionSetNameCollisionRefusal` refuses a `permission` write whose name a DIFFERENT owner already holds, nothing written. It is asked at every door a body reaches `active` through:

- **the save door** (`saveMetaItem`, draft and publish mode), right after the sibling owner judge;
- **the draft→active promotion** (`promoteDraftForPublish`, shared by the per-item publish and `publishPackageDrafts`), on `promoteInto` — a batch publish aborts on it;
- **the restore doors** (review should-fix 2): first in `refuseRestoredBodyTheSaveDoorRefuses`, under `rollbackMetaItem` and `revertCommit`, on the binding the restore lands in (the active row's `package_id`, which `put` keeps; `null` when no active row exists and the package-unbound row is written). A version of a deleted set cannot come back as a second holder of a name a package has taken since.

The save-door check runs before the create precondition, so `If-None-Match: *` cannot smuggle a cross-owner create.

**The owner is the binding the write LANDS IN (review must-fix 1).** The first cut judged the owner judge's binding (`saveWriteBinding`), which reads the store only when the body carries a `packageId`, so the owning package's own plain `?mode=draft` edit (body without `packageId`, no package named) was judged as the environment and refused, although the repository writes that draft into the inherited package (`resolveWriteHead`). The save door now hands the predicate: the named package (for a publish-mode save naming none, the package the package-less address resolved, already on the request); for a draft save naming none, the `into` of the draft address `packagelessDraftAddress` names — the address the door already reads, read here too for the server-stated rewrites it is not read for — and an ambiguous address is refused with the refusal the repository answers it with (`RESOURCE_CONFLICT` / 409, "name the package"); otherwise the package-unbound row (`null`).

**The holders: two readings, met.** The stored active rows by `package_id` (a set published through the metadata door is stored and registered in the registry's bare slot without a package, so only the row says whose it is), and the registry's OWN package-held reading for a set a package ships in code or declares in its install claim (review should-fix 5; ruling letter B on #22371, record 6074838935: one reading of who holds a name). `@objectstack/objectql` exports that reading as `findPackageHeldSecurityCatalogNames(registry)`; metadata-protocol cannot import objectql (objectql depends on it), so the predicate asks the same registry member the export asks, as it already asks the registry's `defaultRecordPageHoldersOf` for the default-record-page rule. A new objectql suite drives the doors over the real `ObjectQL` + `SchemaRegistry` composition, so a rename of that member reds there. The first cut's `getItem` reading (one item, no install claims, a bare-slot stamp read as a package) is gone.

**A package-less row beside exactly one package's row is that package's (review should-fix 6).** #23165's rule for the write address, applied to ownership: such a row is the residue of the direct save before it was re-addressed, so it is not a second owner. The owning package's edit and a write landing in the residue row are accepted; another package is still refused, and its refusal names the package alone.

**Envelope (review should-fix 4).** `NAMESPACE_CONFLICT` / 422, worded as the registry's `SecurityCatalogNameConflictError` ("Security catalog name conflict: … is already held by …", the same rationale sentence), prescription first because a 4xx message is truncated at 500 characters at the REST boundary. The rulings fix this rule's envelope at that code and status on every path, so a client reads one code for the rule whichever door it met. The code is `@objectstack/objectql`'s; `@objectstack/spec`'s `ERROR_CODE_LEDGER` now lists it under `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` too (the `DEFAULT_RECORD_PAGE_CONFLICT` precedent); the `ErrorCode` union is unchanged and no code is minted.

**Faces declared (review should-fix 3).** The changeset's "Who sees it" now names `POST /api/v1/packages/:id/duplicate` (a copied set whose name lacks the source namespace prefix is reported in `failed[]`; remedy: prefix it with your own module prefix) and `os migrate meta --stored --apply` (a re-saved row of a name two owners hold is reported failed until one set is renamed or deleted).

A `patch` changeset ships it for `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` and `@objectstack/spec`.

## Tests

- `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.permission-set-name-cross-package.test.ts` — 17 cases on the storing engine double (doubles recorded in `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json`), each refusal paired with a control through the same door: the save door (both modes, the environment author, the create precondition, an install-claimed name); the owner as the binding the write lands in (the must-fix pin: owner B holds the active set, body without `packageId`, `mode: 'draft'`, no package on the request → `success: true`, draft bound to B; the publish-mode control; the ambiguous draft address); the package-less residue; the promotion (per-item and batch, `failed[].code` = `NAMESPACE_CONFLICT`); the restore door through `rollbackMetaItem` and its control. Shapes a deployment can only hold from before this hardening are staged through the real write path with the predicate switched off for the staging writes alone.
- `packages/objectql/src/protocol-permission-set-name-registry-reading.test.ts` — 4 cases over the real composition (`ObjectQLPlugin` binding the real protocol to a real `ObjectQL` and its `SchemaRegistry`, an in-memory driver): the exported reading names the claimant; another installed package and the environment are refused `NAMESPACE_CONFLICT` / 422 naming it, nothing stored; control.

## Acceptance notes

- `Metadata-protocol: none`: no authorable key, value or type changes; a cross-owner second set was never an authorable capability (the install and cold-boot doors and the Studio dialog already refuse it). The accept-set narrowing is at the metadata HTTP doors, which is why `Clause-②` carries the `(narrowing)` arm while the kind stays `none` and the level `patch`. Re-checked after the envelope change: relative to `main` the doors still go from accepting to refusing, and the ledger row adds no member to the `ErrorCode` union, so the declaration is unchanged.
- The registry seam is structural by necessity (the dependency runs objectql → metadata-protocol). A host registry without the reading member answers no package-held name, as a registry without `getItem` did before; on the one production host the objectql suite above holds it.
- `security-catalog-namespace.ts` (objectql) states the registry does not judge "an environment-catalog save over a package-held name — that path keeps its own answers". Still true: the metadata doors now give that answer, with the registry's envelope. Its header could point at the metadata-protocol predicate; not touched here (no behaviour, outside this diff's files).
- `os migrate security-catalog-overlays` and the cold boot read the bare slot as the environment's; this door reads stored rows by binding. The two meet on the package half (one reading) and differ only on the stored half, which the cold boot cannot see by construction.
